item.title: NOSB Rejects Request to Include Synthetic Polymers in Organics Compost List
item.description: A U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) advisory board—the National Organic Standards Board (NOSB)—rejected a proposal from the Biodegradable Products Institute (BPI) to modify the National List of Allowed and Prohibited Substances (National List). item.title: The Federal Aviation Administration Adopts New Airworthiness Directive for Bombardier Inc. Airplanes
item.description: On February 17, 2026, the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) issued a final rule adopting a new airworthiness directive (AD) for certain Bombardier Inc. airplanes. This new AD requires locking features to be installed on applicable network interfaces to prevent unauthorized network access. FAA seeks 45-day public comment on any written data, views, or arguments associated with this final rule, ending on April 3, 2026. item.description: We previously reported that in December 2025, a food and beverage industry coalition challenged a Texas law requiring food and beverage manufacturers doing business in the state to affix warning labels on products containing any of 44 specific artificial colors, chemicals, and additives. item.title: DC Download-S1 E 11: From Executive Orders to Enforcement: Polsinelli’s 2026 Playbook [Podcast]
item.description: From rapid-fire executive orders to the growing role of AI in agency enforcement, 2026 is already proving to be a consequential year in Washington. In this episode, we welcome Will Vail and explore what comes after the headlines, implementation challenges, litigation trends, appropriations dynamics, and practical strategies for businesses navigating an evolving regulatory landscape.

item.title: Senate Advances SAT Streamlining Act as FCC Continues Its Space Modernization Efforts
item.description: On Feb. 12, 2026, the Senate Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation approved S. 3639, the Satellite and Telecommunications (SAT) Streamlining Act. item.title: Important Changes in CNIPA Service Practice for Madrid Designations
item.description: Key Update The Chinese National Intellectual Property Administration (CNIPA) has stopped copying local Chinese trademark agents on notifications for international trademarks designating China through the Madrid System. Since late last year, CNIPA now serves only the representative recorded with WIPO, or in some cases, the trademark holder directly. item.title: SDNY Addresses Privilege and Work Product Implications of Using Unsecured Public AI Tools
item.description: On February 10, 2026, Judge Jed Rakoff of the Southern District of New York ruled in United States v. Heppner that documents generated through a consumer version of Anthropic’s Claude AI were not protected by the attorney-client privilege or the work-product doctrine under the circumstances presented.
